title: Why you automatically copy other people's body language
hook: You copy people's body language without even knowing it.

narration.text: You copy people's body language without even knowing it.
This is called the chameleon effect, a form of unconscious mimicry.
Our brains are wired to mirror the actions of others.
It helps us understand their emotions and intentions.
This mirroring creates a sense of connection and rapport.
You might notice it when someone crosses their legs after you do.
Or they lean in slightly when you lean in.
It is a subtle dance of non-verbal communication.
Have you ever caught yourself mimicking someone else's movements?

description: Discover the fascinating reason why we often unconsciously imitate the postures and gestures of those around us. This psychological phenomenon, known as the chameleon effect, helps build connection and understanding. Learn how your brain's natural mirroring abilities influence your social interactions.
topic: Why you often imitate the postures and gestures of people you are talking to.
